covers: Speaking and feeding after a stroke. Speaking is expected to improve (improved = yes with a year); feeding is not. Hand weakness is mentioned but walking and dressing must stay empty.
notes: The patient is a 68-year-old who had a left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke in March 2023.
I have been their family physician since 2010.
Since the stroke they have expressive aphasia and dysarthria. They cannot make themselves understood by strangers, and
even family members understand only short phrases. A conversation takes more than three times as long as for someone
of the same age, because they must write words down or point to a picture board. This is the case all or substantially
all of the time. They attend speech-language therapy twice a week and use a tablet communication app.
No medication is taken for the speech impairment.
They also have oropharyngeal dysphagia from the stroke and need a pureed diet with thickened fluids. Weakness in the
right hand means they cannot cut food or open containers. They eat with a weighted spoon and a plate guard.
Each meal takes over an hour, more than three times longer than normal, all or substantially all of the time.
No medication is taken for the feeding impairment.
Both impairments began in 2023 and have lasted more than 12 months. With ongoing therapy, their speech-language
pathologist expects speech to improve by 2027. The feeding impairment is not expected to improve.
Medical records are on file. Under my care from 2010 to present.
